selection_notes: Although several candidates share node numbers or low-FOXP3/TIGIT features, their full primary rules differ and they invoke distinct mechanisms such as T-cell proliferation, chemokine-mediated trafficking, or tumor-associated Treg recruitment.
answer: Primary Zone: Node 8 (FOXP3<=0.26 & CXCR6>=0.5) Mechanistic Rationale: CXCR5 and CXCR7 are chemokine receptors expressed on regulatory T cells (Tregs), which are essential for maintaining self-tolerance and preventing autoimmune disease. The loss of Cxcr7 resulted in increased serum levels of cytokines associated with inflammation and autoimmunity such as IL-2, IL-17A, IFN-γ, and TNFα, while increasing the proportion of Foxp3+ Tregs . It can also regulate lymphocyte trafficking and positioning within the spleen , which is crucial for the maintenance of self-toliterance and prevention of autoimmunity. Literature Confirmed Findings: CXCL13+, HLA-DR+, CD38+ activated DCs and macrophages secrete IL-2. New Testable Mechanisms: Chemokines are important regulators of leukocyte traffickics, but less attention has been paid to the role of chemokines in the development of autoimmune diseases. In particular, the role of CXCR signaling in T cell homeostasis remains understudied. Given the critical role of T cells in the development and progression of autoimmunities, future studies investigating the potential role of Cxcl13/Cxcr5 signaling in modulating T cell function may reveal new therapeutic targets for the treatment of autoimmunate diseases. Secondary Zone: Node18 (FOXR3>=0.25 & NKG7<=-1.4) Mechanistic rationale: NKG2D is a natural killer cell surface protein that binds to its ligands MHC class I chain-related proteins A and B (MICA and MICB) on stressed or tumor cells, leading to the activation of NK cells . Previous study showed that the expression of MICA is significantly up-regulated in CCR5 +/+ CD4+ naïve T cells compared to CCR5 −/− naïve CD4+ cells. Moreover, CCR5 plays a key role in promoting the migration of naive T cells to peripheral tissues, especially to the lungs, where they differentiate into memory T cells. Literature confirmed findings: NK cells play an important role in the clearance of virus-infected cells and cancer cells. They also participate in allograft rejection and transplantation tolerance . Our recent study demonstrated that blocking of the NKG3-CD94 interaction reduced NK cell killing activity against allogeneic lung cancer cells . Therefore, we hypothesize that NK cells may contribute to the clearance and elimination of allogeneic naïve effector T cells in peripheral t issues through the NK3-CD84 pathway. Future studies could use NKG8 antibodies to block the interaction between NKG4 and CD94 and inhibit NK cell cytotoxicity.
